title: Partner status & closure playbook — cache race incident
content:
Purpose:
This is a customer-facing communications playbook for a specific class of incident we saw in eu-west-1: a cache/kv-index race during autoscaling that caused token duplication and occasional corrupted context for ~0.5–1% of streaming chat sessions. Use this doc to: craft concise status updates, prepare a short postmortem summary for external customers, and provide suggested remediation language for accounts and partners.

Notes on tone and audience:
- Primary audience: engineering/product leads at impacted customers and partner integrators.
- Keep initial public status short and readable; include an explicit recovery ETA only when confident.
- Postmortem should be thorough but non-blaming; explain root cause in plain language and list concrete mitigations and monitoring improvements.

Quick status snippets (pick one; paste to status page or partner email):
1) Concise (status page headline):
- Title: Partial corruption of session context for a subset of chat requests in eu-west-1 — service stable, remediation in progress
- Body: Between 2027-05-14T09:12Z and 2027-05-14T11:03Z, a fraction of streaming chat requests in eu-west-1 returned duplicated or out-of-order tokens due to a cache desynchronization during autoscaling. We have applied a rollback/repair and verified normal request behavior; root cause analysis and long-term fixes are underway. No customer data was exfiltrated.

2) Customer-facing detail (email to impacted accounts):
- Impact: Some chat sessions experienced duplicated tokens or truncated context leading to reduced coherence for affected responses. Estimated affected traffic: ~0.5–1% of requests routed to the autoscaled pool in eu-west-1.
- Timeline: We observed the first anomaly at 2027-05-14T09:12Z; mitigation steps started at 09:40Z; normal behavior validated at 11:03Z.
- What we changed: rolled back the autoscaler to the previous stable image, purged KV cache entries on the affected nodes, and disabled the new cache-merge optimization while we investigate.
- Customer action: No immediate action required. If you operate long-lived conversations, consider forcing a short context refresh (send a lightweight noop token) while we deploy extra safeguards (sample script below).

Sample short context-refresh snippet (one-liner example for customers):
- POST /v1/chat/sessions/{session_id}/messages {"role":"system","content":"__context-refresh__"}

Technical root-cause (plain language + short technical addendum):
- Plain language: During an autoscale event, a new node joined the serving pool and attempted to merge a partially populated KV cache. A race in the cache-merge logic allowed stale/inconsistent KV entries to overwrite the active prefix cache for a small subset of sessions, which produced duplicated tokens or truncated continuations for those sessions.
- Technical addendum (for engineering-literate customers):
  - Trigger: new autoscaler heuristic that performed concurrent cache warmup + eager prefix merge.
  - Fault mode: non-atomic merge allowed an older cache segment to replace a newer prefix for certain session keys when timestamps wrapped across the node boundary.
  - Observability: increased 5xx-like anomalies in token sequence validation checks and KV-mismatch traces.

Containment & remediation performed (actions timeline):
- 09:12Z — anomaly detection alerted based on token-sequence checksum deviation.
- 09:18Z — SRE on-call confirmed elevated sequence-checksum failures scoped to eu-west-1 autoscaling events.
- 09:25Z — traffic routing adjusted to prefer warm nodes; new node scale-ups paused.
- 09:40Z — rolled back autoscaler change, pushed cache purge script to all affected nodes.
- 10:15Z — started sampling end-to-end session replays to validate fixes.
- 11:03Z — sampling shows token sequencing within expected bounds; resumed normal autoscale after safer warmup is enabled.

Customer impact summary for partner brief (short bullets):
- Affected region: eu-west-1 only.
- Impact window: ~1h50m (first detection to verified recovery).
- Severity: moderate (coherence degradation for a subset of sessions).
- Data exposure: none detected.
- Recommended immediate action for customers: none required; optional context-refresh if you see persistent degraded sessions.

FAQ (two-line answers to prep partner support responses):
- Q: Did this cause data loss?
  A: No persistent data loss was detected; some responses were poorly formed but session history intact.
- Q: Will this happen again?
  A: We have disabled the unsafe cache-merge path, added stricter sequence validation, and added a canary rollout for the autoscaler; these reduce recurrence risk.
- Q: Do we get credit/compensation?
  A: We'll follow our outage compensation policy for incidents that cross SLA thresholds. For high-impact partners, account teams will reach out proactively.

Postmortem summary template (to paste into customer-facing postmortem):
- Summary: On 2027-05-14, a cache desynchronization during a coordinated autoscale event in eu-west-1 caused duplicated/out-of-order tokens for a minority of streaming chat sessions. The issue affected approximately 0.5–1% of requests routed to the new autoscaled nodes. We mitigated the issue by pausing autoscale, rolling back the autoscaler change, purging affected caches, and validating session integrity. Full recovery verified at 11:03Z.
- Root cause: A non-atomic cache-merge optimization combined with timestamp wrap-around allowed stale cache segments to replace active prefixes during node join.
- Immediate fixes: rolled back autoscaler optimization, deployed cache purge and sequence validators, increased sampling and alerting.
- Long-term actions:
  - Rework cache-merge to be strictly atomic and idempotent (INF-4521).
  - Add pre-join cache-warmup window and deterministic version checks.
  - Improve canary gating for autoscaler changes (smaller ramp, latency/sequence validation gates).
  - Add customer-visible incident tags to the status page for quicker cross-ref.
- Monitoring & verification: new token-sequence checksum metric and KV-merge histogram added; two-week elevated sampling to confirm no regressions.

Suggested customer closure message (short):
- Title: Issue resolved — eu-west-1 chat coherence incident
- Body: We have resolved the issue that affected chat coherence in eu-west-1, rolled back the autoscaler change, and applied fixes. Root cause analysis and long-term remediations are documented; please reach out to your account lead if you saw user-facing impact and want a follow-up.

Suggested outreach cadence and owners:
- Day 0 (within 2 hours): initial concise status page and targeted partner email (owner: on-call CS lead).
- Day 0–1: direct outreach to top impacted partners with incident summary and ETA for postmortem (owner: partner CS manager).
- Day 3: publish customer-facing postmortem and remediation plan (owner: customer-success + incident reviewer).
- Day 7: follow-up with any partners requesting deeper technical calls; offer SRE-led review session.

Open questions / decisions to make in the draft (placeholders to close before publish):
- Confirm exact % of affected traffic (ticket INF-4519 has raw sampling; need final number).
- Confirm compensation threshold cross-check with finance/legal for impacted enterprise customers.
- Decide whether to include anonymized example session snippet in the postmortem (privacy check required).

Internal checklists for publishing:
- [ ] Run legal/privacy review if including session snippets.
- [ ] Confirm all linked Jira/Confluence links are public/customer-safe.
- [ ] Get sign-off from SRE and Product on technical summary wording.
- [ ] CEO/Head of Ops briefing for any top-10 revenue partners impacted.

Appendix: quick copy-paste templates
- Status page short (one paragraph):
  Between 09:12Z and 11:03Z today, a subset of streaming chat requests in eu-west-1 returned duplicated or out-of-order tokens due to a cache synchronization issue during an autoscale event. We rolled back the autoscaler change and purged affected caches; services are operating normally. Investigation and long-term fixes are in progress.
- Partner email subject: Reconciling 2027-05-14 eu-west-1 chat coherence event — initial summary
- Partner email body (short):
  Hello —
  During a routine autoscale event in eu-west-1 you may have observed occasional garbled or repeated tokens in streaming chat responses. We mitigated the issue within 2 hours and have verified recovery; we will follow up with a full postmortem in 72 hours with technical details and planned fixes. If you observed user impact, please reply and we will prioritize a follow-up.

End of draft.

Document history / edits:
- 2027-05-14 created by Priya Nair (initial incident summary).
- 2027-05-16 updated by Ethan Brooks (added timeline details and FAQ).

(Internal shorthand: keep this as the canonical partner-facing draft for cache/kv-style autoscale incidents; do not conflate with routing or model-fallback incidents which require a different message.)
